lines: When concept can impress the self alone,
no other means required — released from bonded
activity, graced by pure knowledge, having taken
the form of the Lord's power, relied on as means,
it brings forth the śākta knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: tatra yadā vikalpaḥ svayam eva saṃskāram ātmani upāyāntaranirapekṣatayaiva kartuṃ prabhavati tadā asau pāśavavyāpārāt pracyutaḥ śuddhavidyānugraheṇa parameśaśaktirūpatām āpanna upāyatayā avalambyamānaḥ śāktaṃ jñānam āvirbhāvayati

lines: This point is settled in the ahnika
that follows next.
sanskrit_cite: tad etac ca nirṇītam anantara eva āhnike

lines: But when the concept leans on another means
for its own impress — taking mind, breath, body,
pot and the rest, limited-formed, as instruments,
reaching subtlety — it brings forth āṇava knowledge.
Therein: mind is meditation-natured; breath,
gross and subtle — the first articulation-natured;
articulation names the five functions of breath;
the subtle, letter-sound-denoted, comes later;
body, arrangement-specific, goes by instrument-sound;
pots and the rest stand external, praised as means
by pit-pot-liṅga worship.
sanskrit_cite: yadā tu upāyāntaram asau svasaṃskārārthaṃ vikalpo 'pekṣate tadā buddhiprāṇadehaghaṭādikān parimitarūpān upāyatvena gṛhṇan aṇutvaṃ prāpta āṇavaṃ jñānam āvirbhāvayati tatra buddhiḥ dhyānātmikā prāṇaḥ sthūlaḥ sūkṣmaś ca ādya uccāraṇātmā uccāraṇaṃ ca nāma pañca prāṇādyā vṛttayaḥ sūkṣmas tu varṇaśabdavācyo vakṣyate dehaḥ saṃniveśaviśeṣātmā karaṇaśabdavācyaḥ ghaṭādayo bāhyāḥ kumbhasthaṇḍilaliṅgapūjādyupāyatayā kīrtayiṣyamāṇāḥ

lines: Here the fitting meditation: that self-luminous
supreme tattva, contained in all tattvas —
meditate it in the knowledge of your own heart,
then meditate the union of knower, instrument
and known, the fire-sun-moon triad, until you
become the great Bhairava-fire, fanned by the
meditation-wind. From that wheel wrapped in
twelve old power-flames, out through some pore-door,
contemplate it resting outside in the graspable self;
and by that rested one, first fill the external
with moon-form in creation's order, then light it
with sun-form in preservation, then dissolve it
in the fire of dissolution, then cause it
unsurpassable-selfhood — meditate.
sanskrit_cite: tatra dhyānaṃ tāvat iha ucitam upadekṣyāmaḥ yat etat svaprakāśaṃ sarvatattvāntarbhūtaṃ paraṃ tattvam uktaṃ tad eva nijahṛdayabodhe dhyātvā tatra pramātṛpramāṇaprameyarūpasya vahnyarkasomatritayasya saṃghaṭṭaṃ dhyāyet yāvat asau mahābhairavāgniḥ dhyānavātasamiddhākāraḥ sampadyate tasya prāktanaśaktijvālādvādaśakaparivṛtasya cakrātmanaḥ cakṣurādīnām anyatamasuṣiradvāreṇa niḥsṛtasya bāhye grāhyātmani viśrāntaṃ cintayet tena ca viśrāntena prathamaṃ tadbāhyaṃ somarūpatayā sṛṣṭikrameṇa prapūritaṃ tataḥ arkarūpatayā sthityā avabhāsitaṃ tato 'pi saṃhāravahnirūpatayā vilāpitaṃ tataḥ anuttarātmatām āpāditaṃ dhyāyet

lines: Thus that wheel stands complete with all
divisions of external things.
Then with that wheel, meditate the residual
habit-states, made as they were.
sanskrit_cite: tato vāsanāśeṣān api bhāvān tena cakreṇa itthaṃ kṛtān dhyāyet

lines: For the unceasing meditator who determines
from his own consciousness the real series of
creation, preservation, dissolution — and creation's
autonomy supreme — at once comes the
Bhairava-state.
sanskrit_cite: evam asya anavarataṃ dhyāyinaḥ svasaṃvinmātraparamārthān sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhāraprabandhān sṛṣṭyādisvātantryaparamārthatvaṃ ca svasaṃvido niścinvataḥ sadya eva bhairavībhāvaḥ

lines: By practice: every desired attainment,
and the rest besides.
Self-luminous, all-self-tattva —
the triad beginning with measure.
Entered within, standing, let him meditate
in the abode of heart-bliss.
That twelve-great-power-ray-wheel-Lord,
all-pervading.
Emerging by ethers outside, meditate it —
bearing the states from creation on.
That mandala swallowing all outer-inner being —
into the self.
Resting, let the yogin contemplate:
thus the spread of self.
sanskrit_cite: viśrāmyan bhāvayed yogī syād evam ātmanaḥ prathā

lines: The summary-verses, these.
Meditation ends here.
When articulating breath: first he rests
in heart-emptiness; then outside, from breath's
arising; then toward external, by apāna's
moon-filling, seeing all-selfness; then
desiring no other; from samāna's arising,
union-rest; from udāna-fire's rise, the
construction of measure and measured.
sanskrit_cite: tatra prāṇam uccicārayiṣuḥ pūrvaṃ hṛdaya eva śūnye viśrāmyati tato bāhye prāṇodayāt tato 'pi bāhyaṃ prati apānacandrāpūraṇena sarvātmatāṃ paśyati tataḥ anyanirākāṅkṣo bhavati tataḥ samānodayāt saṃghaṭṭaviśrāntim anubhavati tata udānavahnyudaye mātṛmeyādikalanāṃ grasate

lines: In its swallowing-fire's pacification,
at vyāna's arising — devoid of every limit,
it flashes.
Thus from emptiness to vyāna: these rests —
own-bliss, blisslessness, supreme-bliss,
brahman-bliss, great-bliss, consciousness-bliss,
six bliss-levels taught; of them one connector,
without rise or set, inner-rest-truth-formed:
world-bliss.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ śūnyāt prabhṛti vyānāntaṃ yā etā viśrāntayaḥ tā eva nijānando nirānandaḥ parānando brahmānando mahānandaḥ cidānanda iti ṣaṭ ānandabhūmaya upadiṣṭāḥ yāsām ekaḥ anusaṃdhātā udayāstamayavihīnaḥ antarviśrāntiparamārtharūpo jagadānandaḥ

lines: Therefore in these articulation-levels,
resting each two-wise or wholly, he wins
rest-tattva — apart from body, breath, the rest.
sanskrit_cite: tat etāsu uccārabhūmiṣu pratyekaṃ dvyādiśaḥ sarvaśo vā viśrāmya anyat taddehaprāṇādivyatiriktaṃ viśrāntitattvam āsādayati

lines: Keep the secret of articulating the
creation-dissolution seed; impress the concept. And in
these rests, each has five states, by the depth
of entry.
sanskrit_cite: tad eva sṛṣṭisaṃhārabījoccāraṇarahasyam anusaṃdadhat vikalpaṃ saṃskuryāt āsu ca viśrāntiṣu pratyekaṃ pañca avasthā bhavanti praveśatāratamyāt

lines: Therein first: bliss, from contact with the
portion of fullness; then arising, a moment, in the
habitual's embodimentlessness; then tremor, as self-
power overpowers, loosening body-identity; then sleep,
from outwardness dissolving.
sanskrit_cite: tatra prāg ānandaḥ pūrṇatāṃśasparśāt tata udbhavaḥ kṣaṇaṃ niḥśarīratāyāṃ rūḍheḥ tataḥ kampaḥ svabalākrāntau dehatādātmyaśaithilyāt tato nidrā bahirmukhatvavilayāt

lines: So the non-self, dissolved into self-being:
from the self's all-pervasiveness the non-self
melts in the self — therefore whirling, from great
pervasion's arising.
sanskrit_cite: ittham anātmani ātmabhāve līne svātmanaḥ sarvamayatvāt ātmani anātmabhāvo vilīyate iti ato ghūrṇiḥ mahāvyāptyudayāt

lines: These are the levels from waking on,
up to the limit past the fourth.
And these levels stand where the triangle-
root-heart's upward kuṇḍalinī-wheel is entered.
So in articulation-rest: the supreme pulsation,
knowable-dissolved-in-rest; the dawning knowable;
the already-dawned — that triad of marks we will
tell at the right time.
sanskrit_cite: evam uccāraviśrāntau yat paraṃ spandanaṃ galitāśeṣavedyaṃ yac ca unmiṣad vedyaṃ yac ca unmiṣitavedyaṃ tad eva liṅgatrayam iti vakṣyāmaḥ svāvasare

lines: And the supreme mark here:
the yogini-heart.
There the primary pulsation-form:
contraction-expansion paired, arising as pair-form,
from gaining the visarga-portion's rest — enough.
sanskrit_cite: tatra mukhyā spandanarūpatā saṃkocavikāsātmatayā yāmalarūpatodayena visargakalāviśrāntilābhāt ity alam

lines: Non-luminous:
here entry.
First in self-knowing, then resting in the
knowable, let him bring the knowable to fullness.
sanskrit_cite: pūrvaṃ svabodhe tadanu prameye viśramya meyaṃ paripūrayeta

lines: Full, here he rests — measurer and measured
distinct; quickly let him withdraw.
sanskrit_cite: pūrṇe 'tra viśrāmyati mātṛmeyavibhāgam āśv eva sa saṃhareta

lines: Pervaded, then he rests: those would be,
with emptiness, the six means-levels.
sanskrit_cite: vyāptyātha viśrāmyati tā imāḥ syuḥ śūnyena sākaṃ ṣaḍupāyabhūmyaḥ

lines: Breath and the rest: not after vyāna;
and dissolved in it, the manifestation from
waking on.
sanskrit_cite: prāṇādayo vyānanapaścimās tallīnaś ca jāgrat prabhṛti prapañcaḥ

lines: Practice-established here, in the abode of
creation-dissolution contemplation, let him grow
before long.
Inner-verses: these.
Articulation ends here.
In this articulation flashes a sound-letter,
almost imitation of the unmanifest; its primary form
is in the creation-dissolution seed — from its
practice, gain of supreme-consciousness. For instance:
in kā, at mā's end, in sācke, in anacke, or
articulated within, remembered — the touch of
consciousness-pulsation, equally distinguished,
complete in disregard of convention; even for those
who keep convention, words that make its meaning,
like mirage and the rest; from the touch of
unsurpassable consciousness, let him unify heart-
throat-lips, the pair of twelve-ends, and heart —
the letter-secret.
sanskrit_cite: asmin eva uccāre sphuran avyaktānukṛtiprāyo dhvaniḥ varṇaḥ tasya sṛṣṭisaṃhārabīje mukhyaṃ rūpaṃ tadabhyāsāt parasaṃvittilābhaḥ tathāhi kādau mānte sācke anacke vā antaruccārite smṛte vā samaviśiṣṭaḥ saṃvitspandasparśaḥ samayānapekṣitvāt paripūrṇaḥ samayopekṣiṇo 'pi śabdāḥ tadarthabhāvakā manorājyādivat anuttarasaṃvitsparśāt ekīkṛtahṛtkaṇṭhoṣṭho dvādaśāntadvayaṃ hṛdayaṃ ca ekīkuryāt iti varṇarahasyam

lines: The white-yellow-and-rest inner letter, born
immediately after inner-touch-contemplation, being
manifested, causes consciousness to be experienced —
so some say.
sanskrit_cite: antaḥsparśadvimarśānantarasamudbhūtaṃ sitapītādyāntaraṃ varṇam udbhāvyamānaṃ saṃvidam anubhāvayati iti kecit

lines: With the expressible absent, from consciousness-
pulsation — by moon-and-sun motion's two checks.
Of those: by equal entry it stands complete —
the letter-form of the consciousness-seed-mass.
The inner-verse, this one.
The letter-rule ends here.
The operation of mudrā-revelation
we will tell next.
